Assistant Professor (ATER) in Economics  
[Université de Lille — FaSEST](https://fasest.univ-lille.fr/)  
[LEM — CNRS UMR 9221](https://lem.univ-lille.fr/en/)

I am an Assistant Professor (ATER) in Economics at the University of Lille and a member of Lille Économie Management (LEM, CNRS UMR 9221).

My research interests include quantitative economics, theoretical economics, search and matching theory, econometrics, and environmental economics.

My current research focuses on the economic and environmental implications of teleworking, including residential location choices, commuting behaviour, mobility patterns, and greenhouse gas emissions.

## Research Interests

- Environmental Economics
- Urban Economics
- Labour Economics
- Search and Matching Theory
- Bid rent models
- Causal inference

## Academic Background

I received my PhD in Economics from Université Savoie Mont Blanc, where my doctoral research focused on Teleworking challenges for the energy transition.

During my doctoral studies, I was a Visiting Researcher at  [ESG–Université du Québec à Montréal (UQAM), Department of Economics](https://economie.esg.uqam.ca/en/) and received advanced training in microeconometrics, public policy evaluation, modern estimation methods and machine learning at the [Microeconometrics and Policy Evaluation Summer School at the Paris School of Economics](https://www.parisschoolofeconomics.eu/en/summer-school/microeconometrics-and-policy-evaluation/).

In 2026, I joined the [Department of Economics & Finance at Florida Gulf Coast University (FGCU)](https://www.fgcu.edu/cob/programs/fin-econ/econbs) as a Visiting Researcher.
